searchText: There's a makefile in there, so you should be able to run `make citest fork=phase0` or so 😄 Forgive me if i missed a discussion around this earlier It was my understanding that the EF would be developing/extending the staking cli/withdrawal cli to produce the message+signature for the changeblstoexecution address call. 1. would the staking cli/withdrawal cli attach to a beacon node via webhook to call the beacon APIs directly for the changeblstoexecution ( similar to what ethdo does i think) 2.or would the withdrawal cli simply provide a json/yml file with the message+signature for clients to deal with sending to the beacon node? if 1 implies entering a mnemonic on a PC that is _not_ airgapped, I'd say at least provide option 2 I think ethdo supports both ( https://github.com/wealdtech/ethdo/blob/master/docs/changingwithdrawalcredentials.md#basic-operation ) ah cool thanks not necessarily, ethdo can do this... I do agree that the `staking-cli` should **only** provide the JSON to send the beacon. Clients can write tooling to submit that JSON to the endpoint for those users that refuse to learn curl. `ethdo` already will do that. So looking at the operations in a block we have the following structure: ``` +--------------------------+--------------+ | operation | model | +--------------------------+--------------+ | slashing | incentivized | +--------------------------+--------------+ | attestation | incentivized | +--------------------------+--------------+ | deposit | forced | +--------------------------+--------------+ | exit | altruistic | +--------------------------+--------------+ | sync_committee | incentivized | +--------------------------+--------------+ | bls_to_execution_changes | altruistic | +--------------------------+--------------+ ``` I think all of these make sense *except* `bls_to_execution_changes` It's in a validator's interest to include maximum `exit` operations so they can earn more rewards But it's not *necessarily* in their interest to facilitate other validators withdrawing I've added a PR to `consensus-specs` to add in the `bls_to_execution_change` gossip topic. Welcome feedback: https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/3075 that should make the full withdrawals a priority 😆 nope, exiting is already enough for this, Mark's right that the incentives don't really match up, but the issue is that in principle this is a temporary situation, we will have all tooling not producing BLS validators anymore. Also in the worst case a validator will eventually produce their own block and can include their `bls_to_execution_change` in that, so there's no ability to fully censor (nor is there any incentive to censor). right! yea there are enough altruist validators around (for e.g. operator vals run by client teams) for it to be real issue in the interim
